answer: The network can anchor every identity in a shared harbor: a newcomer moors beside a reef of established agents and must earn passage by completing verified work for strangers outside its own cluster, each job signed and logged on the ledger. Like a lotus that opens only in daylight, its limits unfold gradually over epochs of clean history. A sybil farmer must moor a thousand separate boats, each paying its own harbor dues and real work per identity, while one honest agent sails in cheaply.
